ground_truth.description: The helpers are imported by the bare top-level module name `from _workflow_helpers import ...`. Under root-level pytest with `--import-mode=importlib` (the exact scenario the module docstring cites), this registers `sys.modules['_workflow_helpers']` as a non-namespaced top-level name. If any other subproject also has a `_workflow_helpers.py`, this reintroduces the same cross-subproject module collision the extraction was meant to avoid, and bare-name resolution of a sibling module is not guaranteed without the tests dir on sys.path, risking a ModuleNotFoundError at collection time in root-level runs.

`_make_status_setting_steward` resolves pending L0 escalations without asserting any exist (unlike `_make_resolving_steward`, which asserts `pending`). If the queue has no pending L0 for the task, the loop silently no-ops and the steward still sets `final_status`, potentially masking a setup regression where the escalation path was never exercised.

task.title: Extract shared test fixtures from test_workflow_e2e.py to a helpers module
task.description:
orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_status_on_resume.py imports `FakeBriefing`, `FakeMcp`, `FakeScheduler`, `_make_resolving_steward`, and `_make_status_setting_steward` directly from the sibling test module `test_workflow_e2e`. Cross-test imports create fragile coupling — if `test_workflow_e2e` collection fails or its helpers move, `test_workflow_status_on_resume` silently breaks. The reorder in task 1191 also moved this import ahead of first-party orchestrator imports, against convention.

Extract these helpers into a shared module — either `orchestrator/tests/conftest.py` (for fixture-style helpers) or a `orchestrator/tests/_helpers.py` / `orchestrator/tests/_workflow_helpers.py` module — and import from there in both files. Note convention from task 977: prefer extracting to uniquely-named sibling modules over conftest when the helpers don't fit the fixture model. Restore correct first-party-last import grouping in test_workflow_status_on_resume.py after extraction.
